# Thinking through this year's plan

I'm 73, been on this land since I was a boy. My wife and I are the only ones here now — the children moved to the city years ago. 4.1 mu isn't much, but at our age it's about all we can handle. I've got to be careful about what I plant because I can't be out there picking cotton all day like I used to.

**How I'll split the land:** I'll put about 2 mu in cotton — that's my cash crop, and the price has been okay. Then 1 mu of millet for us to eat and maybe sell a little, and 1.1 mu of mungbean. The mungbean is good because it doesn't need much fertilizer, the soil likes having it in rotation with cotton, and my wife makes good money selling it at the market. Also mungbean and millet don't need much water or work — important for us.

**Cotton (2 mu):** I'll plant mid-to-late April like always, when the soil warms up. I buy hybrid seed from the agro-shop in town — maybe 40 yuan worth per mu. Before planting I put down about 15 kg of urea and maybe 10 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base. The extension fellow said to split the N, so at squaring I topdress another 5-6 kg urea if the plants look pale. I irrigate twice — once after planting if it's dry, and again around flowering. The well electricity is expensive, so I don't water more than I must. I'll spray for aphids and bollworm — can't skip that or you lose the whole crop. Picking cotton is the hard part; my wife and I do it ourselves in three rounds, takes us weeks.

**Millet (1 mu):** I plant this in late May, early June. Old variety, I saved seed from last year like always. Millet barely needs anything — I'll put maybe 5 kg of urea per mu and that's it. No irrigation, it tolerates dry weather. One weeding with the hoe. Harvest in September. Most we keep to eat.

**Mungbean (1.1 mu):** I plant after the spring rain, maybe early June. Bought seed this year — about 20 yuan per mu. Mungbean fixes its own nitrogen so I don't put any urea on it, just a little phosphorus fertilizer, 3-4 kg per mu. No irrigation unless it really doesn't rain. One weeding. Harvest in August-September, picking the pods as they mature. This is steady income for us — the market in town pays decent for clean mungbean.

Cash is tight. I can't afford to be generous with fertilizer or spray, but I also can't skimp on cotton — lose cotton, lose the year. Mungbean and millet are my insurance: cheap to grow, hard to fail completely.
